items.title: GFCI and light fixture not working
items.body: I have a GFCI on the outside of home that I cannot push the test button to test and I replaced it. A new one is doing the same thing as well not allowed me to test I believe it is hooked up to a switch on the inside of the home and in that same panel there is a dimmer switch that controls a light fixture in the kitchen that is also not working. There are other receptacles in the room that work these two are the only things not working with the GFCI on the outside, and the kitchen light on the inside.

items.title: Replacement light fixture not working
items.body: I have a replacement kitchen led light fixture that is not turning on. Power is there: multimeter shows 121.6 at fixture. Previous fixture obviously worked. There are two three-way switches for the fixture. I believe that I've wired correctly. I've tried two led fixtures. Critique as needed. Do I need to supply more info? Thank you.

items.title: Outdoor light fixture not working
items.body:
I am a newbie with anything electrical so please forgive my ignorance. All of a sudden, my front porch light fixture stopped working. Changing the light bulb didn’t work so I’m trying to figure out if it’s the fixture, the switch or the wiring. I tried installing a new fixture but got a pop and flash and it didn’t work (it’s possible I connected it wrong since I was having trouble getting the wires connected with the wire nuts). So I just put the old fixture back in for now (nothing looks corroded on the fixture).

The box that contains the switch for the exterior light also contains a 3 way switch for my foyer light. The only thing i noticed on the switch is that the ground wasn’t connected- is that an issue? I just replaced the switch (hot, neutral and ground) and bought a multimeter. When I test between the hot and the ground on the new switch, I’m getting 120V. When I test between what I believe to be the neutral and the ground when switch is off I get 0...when switch is on, it reads 120V. When I test between the neutral and the hot, I’m always seeing 0V. I thought this was odd- isn’t there supposed to be voltage when touching the probes to the neutral and hot? Can someone clarify this for me? Thanks in advance. Should I turn off the breaker, pull off the fixture outside and flip the breaker back on and test the wires outside to see if it’s making it outside?

items.title: Ceiling fan light fixture not working
items.body:
On the wall we have a switch for the fan and a dimmer for the lights on the fan. The fan works great -- no issues. The lights randomly stopped working today, though.

Now when I open the the part that had all the wires for the light fixture it had 5 black and 5 white. The light fixture has 4 lights so there is one wire for each light and one is the hot wire coming from the top. Now when this wire isn't connected to anything it shows as hot, but once I connect it to one of the wires going to the light bulb it stops showing as hot. It's like it's grounding it or something. This happens to all of the black wires, if the hot wire touches any of the other wires it stops showing as hot. All of the white wires are still connected together.

Any ideas on why the hot wire stops showing as hot when it connects to the other black wire?

items.title: Halogen to LED conversion on multi-light fixture not working
items.body:
I have a fixture with 4 MR16 (two pin) halogen bulbs. If I replace 2 of the halogen bulbs with LED's all bulbs work. If I replace 3 halogen bulbs with LED's all the bulbs act like a strobe light (not flickering because it is a constant on/off pattern). If I replace all halogen bulbs with LED's none of the bulbs work.

The fixture does not have a dimmer.

items.title: One of two LED Kitchen Light Fixtures Not Working on 3 way circuit
items.body: Recently replaced 2 older light fixtures in our kitchen. The one fixture was failing to light which we took to be the ballast which was too expensive to replace for this old fixture. As a result we chose to replace both lights with new LED fixtures. Both are controlled by a 3-way switch one on each end of the kitchen. The first light we installed works fine from both switches. The second, however, refuses to light though wired identically to the first. Fearing a bad fixture we returned it and replaced with another identical one, but the issue remains. Test meter confirmed power at the box. Could a wall switch still be the problem?

items.title: Replacement light fixture not lighting
items.body: I’m replacing an old light fixture with a new LED one. When I got it all hooked up the light turned on very faintly. I checked the fixture by installing somewhere else and it worked fine. Any ideas?

items.title: Certain light bulbs not working in fixture
items.body:
I have recessed lighting in my eaves outside, 8 in front 4 in the back. Most of them were blown and I bought 12 Great Value Led 8W (60W Equivalent) Daylight Color Frosted Light Bulbs to replace them all so they all match in brightness and color.

After replacing 7 of the front ones, the last one didn't work. I tried 4 different bulbs, none of them worked in the socket. The incandescent 25W that was there worked fine, and I had an older LED I snagged and that worked fine so I left it there. I had all the lights on and from the road, the one bulb was noticeably a different color. I could try to find a similar color and style bulb that is a different brand and try it.

What would cause this particular bulb to not work in this socket? All of the fixtures appear to be identical, all on the same switch, and now all using less wattage than before using LEDs. These bulbs are dimmable and the switch is a dimmer switch, which works fine with the alternate bulb put in.

items.title: Installed new ceiling lighting fixture - now other lights in circuit not working
items.body:
Moved into an old house from 1950s, in Austria. The wiring is fairly old, I assume. In the upstairs master bedroom I replaced the ceiling light fixture today. There are three wires, one blue and two grey - which I’ve never seen before and installed the lighting fixture, after i assumed that one of the grey wires as the Earth wire.

I had to drill two 6mm holes in the ceiling and use plugs for the fixture. Although I didn’t use a wire detector, it didn’t seem like i drilled through any wires. Once i put in a Bulb, the light fixture seems to work fine. But now some of the the lights and outlets that are on the same circuit are no longer working.

I will call an electrician tommorow - but was just wondering if anyone might have an idea what it could be? A short circuit? I left the breaker off in case there is a risk of fire etc., any other safety precautions I could take?

items.title: Ceiling Fan and Light Fixture Don't Work
items.body:
I last used my ceiling fan and light fixture in early January 2024. Both worked properly. The unit is operated with a simple remote control. When I attempted to turn the light fixture on last week, neither the fan nor the light would turn on. I can hear a clicking noise in the unit when I press the remote on both the fan and the light options and I can see a blue light on the remote indicating that the remote is working. I have checked the power switch and turned the circuit breaker off and on. Neither seems to impact the problem.
Wondering if I need a new fan/light unit or if there may be an electrical problem?

items.title: Why Would One Light Fixture Work and Not Another?
items.body:
I'm helping a friend install new outdoor garage lights, and I've run into a problem, which is a real head scratcher. I'm hoping to get some ideas on how I can fix the issue.

A single indoor light switch controls the porch light, and two outdoor lights located on each side of the garage door. I replaced the porch light with a new fixture, and that worked without any problem. I then replaced both garage lights with identical light fixtures, after which they failed to work. I checked, and there was electricity going to the bare wires, and I also checked that there was electricity going to the socket of the new fixture, however, the bulb would not light up for both fixtures. I then reinstalled the old light fixtures, and they worked once again. Both the old and new fixtures are stock outdoor lights from Home Depot.

I would appreciate any thoughts on why one light fixture would work, and another wouldn't, and any suggestions on fixing the problem. Thank you!!

items.title: Light Fixtures will not work, even though I have power
items.body:
I have two pendant light fixtures in my kitchen hooked to 3-way switches. One bulb burned out and while replacing that bulb the other blew out. I've replaced both bulbs, but get nothing. I removed the fixtures from the ceiling and tested the wires and switches with a voltmeter. All good. There is power going to the ceiling boxes and the white & black wires coming from the ceiling. I bought two temporary fixtures to further test it. I have successfully tested those fixtures with the volt meter as well as the bulbs... everything. No fixtures work even though I still have power.

Somehow, once any fixture is hooked to power, it kills it. Nothing happens. What am I missing?

items.title: Porch light over heating and stopped working second light fixture
items.body:
I am by no means an electrician, but for my new light fixture I did follow the following schematic - How should I connect the ground wire for my light fixture?

The old fixture kept burning out the bulb so I replaced it with a nice https://www.lightingdirect.com/heath-zenith-hz-4300-4-light-360-degree-motion-activated-outdoor-flush-mount-ceiling-fixture/p2675820

Was working fine and please note I installed:

  • White to White
  • Black to Black
  • And ground to bare ground wire (Actually ran the ground wire around the screw, which I am not sure if that is correct)

Now after installation the light was working fine, but now a couple of months later the light is glowing on an off (poltergeist) and I took it down and there looks like some brown burn marks. Is it time to call in an electrician?

I have thus turned out the light and not using till I get this resolved. I do not need to burn down our home.

items.title: Why did my ceiling light fixture stop working after adding an outlet on the same circuit?
items.body:
I recently added a receptacle for hanging my TV on the wall. To do it I fished a wire through the wall and attached wires to an existing receptacle that's at a lower level on the same wall.

This is a wall that separated two rooms so there is another receptacle on the opposite end. All white wires and a black wire were joined together, and there was a wire between the two receptacles.

After I added the new wires, the ceiling light fixture in both rooms is not working anymore. I can confirm the bulbs are good, and I also tested it with a line tester and made sure current is reaching the fixture (in the bulb receptor), but no light.

Any other ideas on things I could check?

items.title: Light bulb is intermittently not working
items.body:
I have a room with two non-dimmable light fixtures that are connected.
The first fixture will intermittently work. When I take the bulb out of the first fixture, the second fixture won't work.
Sometimes the first fixture will flicker when turned on, then work fine. Sometimes, it won't turn on. I can immediately turn the switch off, and back on, and it usually works.
The second fixture will not work if the first doesn't work
